relevant_findings.summary: Porch ceiling (veranda ceiling) is the overhead horizontal surface on an open or enclosed porch structure. Distinct from soffit (enclosed eave underside) in that porch ceilings are typically sheltered from direct weather by the porch roof, cover a habitable area, and do not have attic ventilation concerns. Common substrates: tongue-and-groove (T&G) boards, beadboard panels, plywood sheets, and fiber cement panels. No vinyl substrate — porch ceilings are structural/aesthetic elements not clad with vinyl soffit panels.

Porch ceiling work is 100% overhead, same as soffit. Production rate reduction of 25-35% from vertical baselines applies to all overhead tasks. Fatigue, gravity-fed drip management, and awkward access angles reduce efficiency. Extension poles are the primary tool for brush/roll overhead application.

relevant_findings.topic: No vent type constraint — spray always eligible
relevant_findings.summary: Unlike soffit, porch ceilings do NOT have attic ventilation perforations. There is no FM-001 attic vent contamination risk. Spray application is always eligible on porch ceiling regardless of panel construction. This removes the soffit_vent_type configuration dimension and the FAC_SFIT_VENT_COMPLEXITY modifier entirely.

Porch ceiling panel types: (1) tg_board — traditional tongue-and-groove boards (3.5-5.5 inch), (2) beadboard — narrow-profile T&G panels with decorative bead profile (similar groove complexity to T&G), (3) solid_panel — plywood sheets or fiber cement panels. Beadboard has the same 20% joint complexity overhead as standard T&G boards because the bead grooves require brush-in work. Both T&G and beadboard require brush work in grooves even when spraying.

relevant_findings.topic: Sheltered surface — reduced UV and weathering
relevant_findings.summary: Porch ceilings are doubly sheltered — under the porch roof AND protected from direct rain/wind. Less UV exposure than soffit (which is under eaves but exposed to reflected light). This means longer coating life but higher mildew risk in humid climates (trapped moisture, limited air circulation, no UV sterilization). Mildew-resistant paint formulation is important, especially on north-facing porches.

Porch ceilings can be at various heights: standard single-story porch (8-10 ft), elevated porch (raised foundation, 10-14 ft), two-story veranda/wraparound porch (16-22 ft). Height drives FAC_EXT_ACCESS modifier: ground (low porch, extension pole reach), ladder (standard porch), scaffold (elevated/two-story porch), lift (rare, very high veranda). Porch ceiling may be higher than typical soffit due to elevated porch floor and tall porch columns.

Porch ceiling adjacent surfaces: (1) soffit_field — may be continuous with soffit at porch roof eave, same color typical, (2) ext_trim_fascia — fascia board at porch roof edge, (3) porch_floor — below (drip protection zone), (4) wall_field — house wall at porch attachment, (5) porch columns/posts — trim elements. Cut-in work at fascia and wall junctions. Often same color as soffit — when continuous, edge work at transition is minimal.

relevant_findings.topic: No vinyl substrate for porch ceiling
relevant_findings.summary: Porch ceilings are NOT clad with vinyl panels. Vinyl soffit panels are specific to enclosed eave soffits. Porch ceilings use wood (T&G, beadboard, plywood) or fiber cement panels. This eliminates the vinyl substrate path, bonding primer system, and solar-reflective finish system from the soffit spec.

relevant_findings.topic: Traditional haint blue porch ceiling color
relevant_findings.summary: Many porch ceilings are painted in traditional 'haint blue' (sky blue/pale blue-green) or white/off-white. This is relevant for sheen selection (flat to satin, same as soffit) and material selection (standard latex with mildewcide). The blue tradition does not affect production rates or spec structure but is a common color choice that estimators should expect.

Protection zones for porch ceiling: (1) porch_floor — directly below, catches all drips from overhead work (CRITICAL), (2) porch_furniture — seasonal furniture, planters, swings may need covering or removal, (3) ext_light_fixture — porch ceiling-mounted fixtures (ceiling fans, pendant lights, recessed cans), (4) ext_fascia_adjacent — fascia at porch roof edge when already finished, (5) wall_adjacent — house wall at porch attachment when already finished. Porch floor is the primary protection zone — all drips fall onto it.

scope_definition.measurement_rule: Net paintable porch ceiling area in square feet. Porch width x porch length (or perimeter-based for wraparound). Excludes ceiling fan/fixture openings.

substrates.description: Tongue-and-groove boards (cedar, pine, fir), beadboard panels, plywood sheets
substrates.prep_requirements: 80-120 grit sand for adhesion. T&G/beadboard grooves require hand-sanding. Tannin spot-prime knots on cedar/redwood.
substrates.primer_path: 100% acrylic exterior primer (full field prime). Tannin spot-prime for knots on cedar/redwood.

substrates.description: HardieSoffit-style fiber cement panels used for porch ceiling
substrates.prep_requirements: Scuff sand factory-primed panels (150 grit). Seal field-cut edges to prevent moisture wicking.
substrates.primer_path: Acrylic primer on factory-primed FC (MANDATORY field prime). Alkali-resistant primer on bare FC (pH 13.0).

excluded_substrates.reason: Vinyl soffit panels are not used for porch ceiling applications. Porch ceilings are structural/decorative elements using wood or fiber cement. No bonding primer or solar-reflective finish system needed.

configuration_dimensions_proposed.notes: QT5 excluded — porch ceiling is a large-area overhead field surface, not fine millwork. QT2 is economy (single finish coat). QT3 is standard (2 finish coats). QT4 is premium (interstage sand, systematic inspection).
Wood (T&G, beadboard, plywood) or fiber cement panels. No vinyl.
Both methods always eligible — no vent type gating (unlike soffit). Spray is always an option on porch ceiling. spray_backroll NOT valid — overhead back-rolling is impractical.
Flat and satin only for overhead surfaces. Per Exterior_Color_Sheen_Configuration_Doctrine: overhead surfaces use flat or satin. No semi-gloss or gloss.

T&G boards and beadboard both have groove joint complexity (~20% labor overhead). Beadboard has narrow-profile bead grooves — same penalty as T&G. Solid panel (plywood, fiber cement) has no joint penalty.

modifier_catalog.name: Overhead Work Penalty
modifier_catalog.application: BAKED_INTO_BASE_RATES — not applied as a stacking modifier. All base rates pre-reduced by 25-35% from vertical baselines.
modifier_catalog.source: RF-002, sibling SF_SOFFIT_EXT_NC_v1 overhead rate design

modifier_catalog.name: T&G / Beadboard Joint Complexity
modifier_catalog.application: Stacking multiplier on brush/roll application and wood sand prep tasks. T&G and beadboard both have groove joint complexity.

modifier_catalog.name: Height/Access Modifier
modifier_catalog.application: Stacking multiplier on all overhead tasks. Reuse FAC_EXT_ACCESS from sibling exterior specs.

material_systems_proposed.name: Exterior Acrylic Primer for Wood/FC Porch Ceiling
material_systems_proposed.notes: 100% acrylic exterior primer for (1) bare wood porch ceiling (full prime) and (2) factory-primed fiber cement (field prime MANDATORY per Hardie warranty). Same product as soffit primer but porch-ceiling-specific system ID.

material_systems_proposed.name: Alkyd/Shellac Spot Primer for Tannin Knots on Wood Porch Ceiling
material_systems_proposed.notes: Spot-applied to visible knots on tannin-rich species (cedar, redwood). Prevents tannin bleed-through — especially visible on flat white and haint blue porch ceilings.

material_systems_proposed.name: Alkali-Resistant Primer for Bare Fiber Cement Porch Ceiling
material_systems_proposed.notes: Required for bare/damaged fiber cement porch ceiling panels (pH 13.0). Prevents saponification.

material_systems_proposed.name: Standard Exterior Acrylic Porch Ceiling Paint
material_systems_proposed.notes: 100% acrylic exterior with mildewcide. Flat to satin. QT2: single coat. QT3: 2 coats. Mildew-resistant formulation critical for sheltered porch ceiling.

material_systems_proposed.name: Premium Exterior Acrylic Porch Ceiling Paint
material_systems_proposed.notes: Premium materials (SW Emerald, BM Aura). 2 coats. Light intercoat sand. Mildew-resistant formulation.

protection_zones_proposed.description: Porch floor directly below ceiling work — primary drip zone
protection_zones_proposed.notes: CRITICAL for overhead work. All drips fall directly onto porch floor. Canvas drop cloths for non-slip crew traffic.

protection_zones_proposed.description: Porch furniture, planters, and swings below ceiling work area
protection_zones_proposed.notes: Cover or remove before any overhead work begins. Plastic sheeting over items that cannot be removed.

protection_zones_proposed.description: Porch ceiling-mounted fixtures — ceiling fans, pendant lights, recessed cans
protection_zones_proposed.notes: Ceiling fans are common on porch ceilings — remove blades if possible, or mask mounting plate and blade edges. Pendant lights: bag fixture, protect chain/wire.

protection_zones_proposed.description: Fascia board at porch roof edge — protect when already finished
protection_zones_proposed.notes: Tape + masking film at fascia-ceiling junction when fascia is already painted.

protection_zones_proposed.description: House wall at porch attachment — protect when already finished
protection_zones_proposed.notes: Tape at ceiling-to-wall junction when house siding/wall is already painted.

adjacent_surfaces.notes: Porch ceiling may be continuous with eave soffit — often same color. Minimal edge work at transition.
Fascia at porch roof edge. Trim color. Cut-in required.
Below porch ceiling. Different material/color. No cut-in (vertical separation).
House wall at porch attachment. Body color. Cut-in required at ceiling-to-wall junction.
Porch columns/posts. Trim or body color. Cut-in at column-to-ceiling junction.

risk_analysis.topic: Tannin bleed-through on wood porch ceiling
risk_analysis.description: Cedar and redwood T&G/beadboard porch ceiling boards bleed tannins through water-based coatings. Brown staining is highly visible on flat white and haint blue finishes.
risk_analysis.mitigation: Spot-prime all visible knots with alkyd or shellac stain blocker before full acrylic primer.

risk_analysis.topic: Mildew growth on sheltered porch ceiling
risk_analysis.description: Porch ceilings are doubly sheltered (under roof, protected from rain) with limited air circulation. Ideal mildew habitat, especially on north-facing and shaded porches in humid climates.
risk_analysis.mitigation: Use paint with mildewcide additive. Clean porch ceiling with mildewcide solution before painting. Ensure adequate porch ventilation.

risk_analysis.description: Overhead application causes visible drips and sags. Excess material runs to fascia/wall junctions or drips onto porch floor.
risk_analysis.mitigation: Apply thin coats overhead. Back-brush immediately after rolling. Use extension pole for consistent pressure.

risk_analysis.topic: Edge wicking on fiber cement panels
risk_analysis.description: Unsealed field-cut edges on fiber cement porch ceiling panels absorb moisture via cellulose capillaries.
risk_analysis.mitigation: Seal ALL field-cut edges with end-cut sealer before or immediately after installation.

risk_analysis.topic: Ceiling fan interference with spray application
risk_analysis.description: Porch ceiling fans create complex masking geometry. Fan blades, mounting plates, and electrical connections must be protected.
risk_analysis.mitigation: Remove fan blades before painting if possible. If not removable, mask blades and mounting plate thoroughly. Consider brush/roll around fan area even when spraying the field.

risk_analysis.topic: Factory primer degradation on fiber cement
risk_analysis.description: Factory primer on fiber cement panels degrades if exposed beyond 180 days.
risk_analysis.mitigation: Field-prime and paint within 180 days of installation.

assumptions.value: 10% additional material waste for overhead application

assumptions.source: Beadboard grooves are functionally equivalent to T&G grooves for painting purposes
assumptions.note: No specific doctrine for beadboard joint complexity. Derived from T&G analogy.

assumptions.value: 8-22 ft range (standard single-story to two-story veranda)
Vinyl soffit panels not used for porch ceilings

uncertainty_flags.description: Beadboard 1.20x modifier is assumed equal to T&G. Beadboard may have slightly different groove geometry (narrower, more grooves per linear foot) but the painting technique is the same.
uncertainty_flags.action: Flag for field calibration. Compare brush-in time on beadboard vs standard T&G on same project.

uncertainty_flags.description: Ceiling fan masking time is estimated based on general fixture masking rates. Actual time depends on fan complexity (3 vs 5 blades, light kit, etc.).
uncertainty_flags.action: Track ceiling fan masking time separately from standard fixture masking.
